milestones.title: Establish the migration contract
acceptance_criteria: Availability, rollback and recovery decisions are recorded or explicitly unresolved.
Source inventory and compatibility criteria identify whether downstream implementation may begin.

milestones.title: Implement compatible PostgreSQL persistence
acceptance_criteria: PostgreSQL preserves schema constraints, stored representations and atomic revision behavior.
All runtime consumers await storage completion and publish events only after commit.
Coordinated mutation locking covers database and asset filesystem changes.

milestones.title: Provide verified migration and recovery
acceptance_criteria: Source and migrated target match project and asset counts, row hashes and file hashes.
A complete PostgreSQL backup restores into an isolated target with matching content.
Incomplete backups and incompatible recovery paths fail closed.

milestones.title: Integrate deployment and demonstrate acceptance
acceptance_criteria: Deployment and rollback procedures check store compatibility and readiness before switching.
Isolated rehearsals verify migration, consumer behavior and recovery against resolved decision gates.
Unverified external compatibility and unmet availability bounds remain explicit acceptance blockers.

tasks.title: Resolve persistence and operational gates
tasks.objective: Produce an executable migration contract or explicit blockers covering availability, recovery, source inventory and client compatibility; do not infer owner decisions.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Provisional estimate for a bounded contract and inventory review, excluding owner waiting time. No comparable history exists; actual data and operational decisions are unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: D1 records permitted interruption, draining, retry/session behavior and measurable cutover bounds; uninterrupted writes require a revised capture/replay plan.
D2 distinguishes pre-write SQLite rollback from post-write PostgreSQL-compatible rollback; required reverse migration triggers replanning.
D3 records PostgreSQL version, connectivity, TLS, privileges, backup retention, recovery objectives and compatible release requirements without selecting a hosting service.
D4 inventories source schema, volume, writers, encoding, assets and consumer evidence before operational execution.
Unanswered decisions remain blockers for T2 through T8 rather than presumed approval.
The compatibility matrix specifies revision-before-no-op precedence, import flags, errors, snapshots, asset URLs and committed events.

verification.value: Review docs/persistence-migration.md against SPEC.md and inspected persistence, consumer and deployment sources.
verification.purpose: Confirm the migration branch and acceptance boundaries are explicit.
verification.expected: Each D1-D4 item has evidence or an unresolved blocker; no downtime, reverse-migration exclusion or external compatibility is presented as approved.

complexity.justification: Migration decisions connect database semantics, external consumers and operational availability.

scope.justification: The research result is one bounded persistence migration contract.

duration.justification: Existing deployment and contract documents bound the initial review work.
evidence: assumption:Source inventory and owner decision latency remain unknown.

risk.justification: Incorrect migration assumptions can lose data or violate availability.

coupling.justification: T2 and T7 consume the persistence-contract and cutover-recovery-contract decisions.

confidence.justification: Repository behavior is visible but production data and recovery objectives are unknown.
evidence: assumption:No production inventory or owner answers are supplied.

tasks.title: Add PostgreSQL connections and versioned schema
tasks.objective: Provide asynchronous PostgreSQL connections and atomic versioned migrations preserving the existing data representation and database constraints after T1 resolves the execution gates.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Provisional estimate for pool configuration, a two-table schema, migration locking and focused tests. Existing schema is inspected; PostgreSQL environment choices depend on T1. No historical timing evidence is available.
acceptance_criteria: The pool requires explicit PostgreSQL configuration, redacts secrets and never falls back silently to SQLite.
Versioned migrations serialize concurrent initialization, commit schema and ledger together, reject newer schemas and roll back failure.
Projects and assets preserve primary keys, unique external keys and relative paths, required fields, JSON validity and cascading foreign keys.
IDs, timestamps and data_json retain their original text representation; numeric mappings reject unsupported ranges instead of truncating.
Readiness checks connectivity and the expected schema version; pool and transaction clients close reliably.
Database tests cover constraints, repeated initialization, concurrent initialization and failed migration rollback.

verification.purpose: Exercise new PostgreSQL schema, connection and migration tests against disposable storage.

complexity.justification: PostgreSQL schema initialization must replace SQLite PRAGMA migration and readiness semantics.

scope.justification: The foundation adds one storage module and schema without converting application consumers.

duration.justification: Two existing tables bound schema translation and focused database testing.

risk.justification: Schema coercion or missing constraints can corrupt migrated project and asset content.

coupling.justification: T3 consumes the postgres-schema and asynchronous connection contract.

confidence.justification: The complete SQLite schema is inspected while deployment parameters await T1.

tasks.title: Port repositories with atomic revision semantics
tasks.objective: Make project and asset repositories asynchronous while preserving committed snapshots, no-op behavior and conflict semantics under independent PostgreSQL connections.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Provisional estimate includes both repositories and focused concurrency tests. Source methods are short, but translating SQLite write serialization requires careful multi-connection verification. No comparable execution history exists.
acceptance_criteria: All repository methods return promises and transactions use one checked-out client with rollback and release on failure.
Mutations serialize by external key including absent-key imports; the revision check occurs before no-op comparison.
New records start at revision one; changed updates increment once; unchanged name, description and serialized data preserve revision and timestamps.
Two changed updates using one revision produce one commit and one conflict carrying the committed currentRevision.
Imports preserve created and changed flags, missing imports require expectedRevision zero, and existing stale imports conflict.
Missing records preserve NotFoundError behavior and duplicate creates retain the current generic-error contract.
Lists preserve descending updated_at ordering without introducing a new tie-order promise; asset metadata preserves uniqueness and foreign keys.

verification.purpose: Verify repository behavior, independent-connection races, stale no-ops and transaction rollback.

complexity.justification: Revision and absent-key import races require translating SQLite transaction serialization.

scope.justification: Changes concentrate in two repositories and their focused tests.

duration.justification: Existing repository methods and one revision test bound implementation and test expansion.

risk.justification: Incorrect conflict handling can overwrite client edits or issue false successful revisions.

coupling.justification: T4 must await the repository-api promises and preserve their errors.

confidence.justification: Mutation branches are fully inspected but concurrent PostgreSQL behavior needs new tests.

tasks.title: Await storage across API and asset consumers
tasks.objective: Preserve HTTP, WebSocket and asset behavior while awaiting asynchronous storage and exposing a coordinated mutation barrier for consistent backup.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Provisional estimate covers five runtime consumers, a mutation barrier and failure-path tests. All consumers were inspected; filesystem/database interleaving adds uncertainty. No measured precedent exists.
acceptance_criteria: HTTP handlers await repository and asset calls and retain response bodies, status codes, validation and authentication behavior.
Revision and deletion events publish only after committed changes; failed or unchanged mutations emit no revision event.
Failed asynchronous metadata insertion removes the newly written asset file; upload/delete interleaving cannot leave committed metadata pointing to a deleted file.
Every API mutation holds the shared advisory barrier across its SQL and filesystem effects; exclusive backup locking drains these operations.
WebSocket upgrades await existence checks and handle disconnects or rejected lookups without unhandled promises.
Startup awaits storage readiness, readyz returns 503 on storage failure, and shutdown drains requests before pool closure.
No runtime server path opens SQLite after conversion; browser API types and canonical contract schemas remain unchanged.

verification.purpose: Detect asynchronous signature mismatches across storage consumers and workspace types.
Exercise HTTP errors, event ordering, readiness, assets and upgrade failure paths.

complexity.justification: Await propagation changes HTTP, socket and filesystem failure ordering across components.

scope.justification: Async conversion spans application routes, server lifecycle, sockets and asset services.

duration.justification: Inspected route and service call sites bound the conversion and failure-case matrix.

risk.justification: Premature responses or incomplete asset cleanup can break client consistency and lose files.

coupling.justification: T6 relies on mutation-barrier coordination across all converted mutation paths.

confidence.justification: Runtime callers are inspected but asynchronous asset races lack existing coverage.

tasks.title: Build repeatable migration and content verification
tasks.objective: Import a consistent SQLite snapshot and asset inventory into isolated PostgreSQL with exact row and file verification, safe retries and no source mutation.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Provisional estimate for a bounded two-table migration, reusable manifests and fault tests. Production volume, source anomalies and the availability strategy remain T1 prerequisites; this is not a migration-duration prediction.
acceptance_criteria: Source acquisition uses a consistent SQLite backup after the approved writer fence and drain; source schema and data are never modified.
Preflight validates schema version, SQLite integrity, foreign keys, target-compatible values and asset path, length and SHA-256.
Projects precede assets in an atomic import into an empty isolated target; all source columns including IDs, revisions and timestamps are preserved.
Row hashes encode fixed-column typed arrays as UTF-8 JSON, preserve raw JSON text and use primary-key byte order for deterministic table aggregation.
Both table counts, per-row hashes, aggregate hashes, asset bytes and representative API snapshots match before success is reported.
Invalid data, missing files or mismatch abort without skipping rows; interrupted attempts roll back and retries never truncate an unknown target.
Tests cover empty and Unicode data, incompatibilities, target collisions, interruption and deliberate content tampering.

verification.purpose: Verify migration counts and hashes, source preservation and failure-safe reruns.

complexity.justification: Migration must reconcile SQLite rows, PostgreSQL constraints and separately stored asset bytes.

scope.justification: The migration command includes source validation, import, verification and recoverable failure behavior.

duration.justification: Two tables limit implementation size while content manifests and fault cases require dedicated work.
evidence: assumption:Production record counts and source anomalies are not supplied.

risk.justification: Incomplete source capture or coercion could silently discard existing project and asset content.

coupling.justification: T6 reuses content-manifest outputs and T7 consumes verified migration results.

confidence.justification: Schema is known but actual source volume and data compatibility remain unverified.
evidence: assumption:No production database or asset inventory was available.

tasks.title: Implement consistent backup and guarded restore
tasks.objective: Produce complete PostgreSQL and asset recovery bundles and restore them into isolated targets with integrity checks and explicit storage compatibility boundaries.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Provisional estimate includes coordinated dumps, manifests, guarded restore and corruption tests. Recovery objectives, PostgreSQL tooling version and permitted write blocking depend on T1. No restore timing has been measured.
acceptance_criteria: Backup holds the exclusive mutation barrier while collecting a compatible PostgreSQL dump and asset copy, preserving one consistent recovery state.
Bundles record store, schema, release, row manifests and asset hashes; metadata precedes checksum generation and a completion marker is written last.
Dump or copy failure leaves a rejected partial bundle, returns failure and releases all locks and connections.
Restore rejects corrupt, incomplete, unsupported or wrong-store bundles and targets only an empty isolated database and asset directory.
Restored table counts, row hashes, file hashes and API reads match the recorded recovery point.
The procedure distinguishes legacy SQLite recovery from PostgreSQL recovery and never treats code rollback as automatic data restoration.
Pre-write SQLite rollback and post-write PostgreSQL-compatible rollback follow D2; disaster-recovery limits remain bounded by D3.

verification.purpose: Exercise backup consistency, interrupted dumps, corrupted bundles and verified isolated restores.

complexity.justification: Backup consistency spans PostgreSQL snapshots, mutation coordination and mutable filesystem assets.

scope.justification: Recovery requires a complete backup producer and guarded restore consumer.

duration.justification: Existing backup structure provides a starting point but restore and corruption coverage are absent.

risk.justification: An apparently successful incomplete backup can make subsequent recovery lose data.

coupling.justification: T7 consumes backup-format and cutover-recovery-contract before deployment or rollback changes.

confidence.justification: Existing backup behavior is inspected while acceptable recovery windows and tooling remain undecided.
evidence: assumption:Recovery time and recovery point objectives are not supplied.

tasks.title: Update deployment and rollback safeguards
tasks.objective: Make deployment and rollback scripts enforce verified migration, readiness, writer fencing and release/store compatibility without executing a production switch.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Provisional estimate covers inspected Docker and EC2 script changes plus runbook updates. Infrastructure capabilities and downtime limits depend on T1; remote deployment time is excluded and unmeasured.
acceptance_criteria: Deployment configuration supplies explicit PostgreSQL connectivity and compatible backup tools while retaining asset and backup persistence and private API exposure.
Preflight checks connectivity, schema/release compatibility, required privileges, available storage and restore evidence without logging secrets.
The serving store's compatible tool creates the pre-cutover backup before candidate activation.
Cutover follows the resolved D1 fence/drain, snapshot, import/verify, readiness/API probe, routing and write-enable sequence.
Persisted phase evidence identifies the authoritative store and first PostgreSQL-write boundary; failures do not activate an unverified target.
Rollback checks store compatibility before changing the release pointer and rejects stale SQLite activation after PostgreSQL writes.
Documentation states interruption, session and WebSocket effects and abort/recovery steps; unresolved D1-D3 gates prevent operational use.

verification.value: Review Dockerfile, Compose, deploy/preflight/rollback scripts and runbooks against the resolved migration contract.
verification.purpose: Check local configuration and control-flow safeguards without invoking remote operations.
verification.expected: No switch precedes verification and readiness; rollback cannot select an incompatible store or release; credentials stay out of logs.

verification.purpose: Exercise deployment-stage and rollback-boundary failure injection in the acceptance harness.

complexity.justification: Cutover ordering connects serving-release backups, verified migration, routing and rollback state.

scope.justification: Deployment changes span container configuration, three operational scripts and associated documentation.

duration.justification: Existing short deployment scripts bound edits but new failure controls require rehearsal support.

risk.justification: Incorrect release activation can interrupt availability or route writes to obsolete data.

coupling.justification: T8 consumes api-deployment safeguards and T6 supplies compatible recovery artifacts.

confidence.justification: Scripts are inspected but actual PostgreSQL infrastructure and cutover tolerances remain unavailable.

tasks.title: Add acceptance rehearsals and consumer regressions
tasks.objective: Produce reproducible isolated evidence for migration integrity, unchanged client behavior and recovery, retaining explicit product and external-consumer evidence gaps.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Provisional estimate for integrated fixture and failure rehearsals plus evidence documentation. Local consumer behavior is inspected; production-scale timings and the absent MCP consumer remain unknown.
acceptance_criteria: Isolated migration fixtures prove complete project and asset counts, raw-content hashes and asset file hashes before and after restart.
HTTP and WebSocket suites preserve snapshots, validation/auth errors, import flags, committed event ordering and asset delivery.
Independent-connection races prove one winning changed update per revision, stale no-op conflicts and correct concurrent import behavior.
Failure injection covers unavailable storage, commit failure, upload/delete races, incomplete backups, checksum tampering and each cutover boundary.
Pre-write SQLite rollback and post-write compatible PostgreSQL code rollback retain the authoritative data; restored bundles match their recorded recovery point.
Browser create/edit/conflict/delete/upload/reconnect flows are exercised; bearer-token API checks do not claim unavailable MCP consumer acceptance.
Measured rehearsal interruption and recovery are compared with D1 and D3; unmet limits or unresolved gates block acceptance.
Test setup fails clearly when disposable PostgreSQL or required artifacts are missing; no required migration test silently skips.

verification.purpose: Run migration, recovery, deployment-failure and client protocol acceptance suites.
Retain the existing canonical import validation behavior.
Check final workspace types after persistence and consumer conversion.

verification.purpose: Evaluate product behavior and measured rehearsal bounds separately from automated test results.
verification.expected: Browser flows retain visible behavior, every integrity comparison matches, operational measurements meet resolved bounds and external MCP compatibility remains explicitly unverified.

complexity.justification: Acceptance combines concurrency, browser protocol behavior and multi-stage recovery failure cases.

scope.justification: Regression coverage spans repository, HTTP, sockets, assets and deployment recovery boundaries.

duration.justification: The single existing repository test requires substantial integration fixture and scenario expansion.

confidence.justification: Local consumers and test scripts are inspected while external consumers and production scale remain unknown.

interfaces.title: Asynchronous repository and transaction contract
inputs: Project identities, external keys, expected revisions and validated project data.
Asset metadata and PostgreSQL transaction connections.
outputs: Promises resolving to committed snapshots, changed/created flags, asset metadata or existing typed errors.
invariants: One transaction connection owns each mutation through commit or rollback.
No-op writes preserve revision and timestamps.
Public response and error shapes remain unchanged.
integration_criteria: HTTP and WebSocket callers await completion and publish only committed changes.
Concurrent changed writes at one revision yield one success and one conflict.
Migrated rows produce equivalent API snapshots.

interfaces.title: Coordinated database and asset mutation barrier
inputs: API mutations spanning PostgreSQL and asset filesystem effects.
An exclusive backup request using the same advisory-lock namespace.
outputs: Shared mutation completion or an exclusive interval with all mutations drained.
invariants: Every writer participates for the entire database and filesystem mutation.
Backup dump and asset copy occur inside the exclusive interval.
Failures release locks and leave no complete marker on partial bundles.
Blocking behavior must comply with the resolved D1 and D3 decisions.
integration_criteria: Concurrent upload/delete attempts cannot make a completed backup reference missing files.
Interrupted backup releases the barrier and subsequent valid mutations can complete.

interfaces.title: Migration and recovery content manifests
inputs: Consistent source rows with every stored column and an asset file inventory.
Store identity, schema version and source snapshot identity.
outputs: Per-table row counts, deterministic per-row and aggregate SHA-256 values, and asset size/hash entries.
Explicit verification success or a failing mismatch report.
invariants: Hashes preserve raw JSON and timestamp text using fixed-column typed encoding and primary-key byte ordering.
Missing, extra or changed rows and files prevent migration or restore acceptance.
Verification does not mutate the source or silently coerce unsupported content.
integration_criteria: SQLite source, PostgreSQL target and isolated restore produce matching inventories.
Deliberate row or asset tampering fails verification and prevents activation.
